findings.text: the deliverable lists `_positive_seconds` in `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py` among the hand-parsers, and the catch-all ("any other site in reckon/ that parses a duration from the environment by hand is migrated too") pulls it in, but its callers `_deadline_seconds` (reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:76-88) and `_landing_grace_seconds` (:90-92) rely on its `None` return as "unset, try the next level" to walk a three-level fallback chain (DEADLINE_ENV → READ/WRITE_DEADLINE_ENV → constant); the new function's contract returns a duration on unset, never a sentinel, so migrating it — or its callers — silently collapses the chain to one level

findings.text: the deliverable says each site "calls it with the bound its own docstring states", but `stop_derivation_budget` (coordinator_obligations.py:169) and `_settle_grace_default` (crew_follow_commands.py:469) state no bound in their docstrings, and the two rules given (a grace may be zero, inclusive; a lease is zero, exclusive) classify neither a "budget" nor whether a settle grace may be zero, so the worker must invent the bound and its inclusivity for those two sites
